selection: 5 rows that still fire the gate, 9 remaining tier-A defined terms, and 26 core clause-4-to-10 and risk concepts. Chosen to be the block a Foundation candidate meets first, not a sample.
style_applied: ISO defined term an item can test on the definition -> both halves, definitional part written from scratch. Plain-English name -> teaching-move-only. Avoided: a pointer with no antecedent, and an absolute the row's own example contradicts.
citation_rows_for_full_read: leadership-commitment - clause 5.1, and the count of eight

citations_verified_before_sending.instrument: direct extraction from indexed ISO/IEC 27001:2022, main body only (Annex A excluded after the shadowing fix), with a self-test
citations_verified_before_sending.5.1: a) to h) - EIGHT lettered demonstrations. Confirmed.
citations_verified_before_sending.5.2: b) includes information security objectives (see 6.2) or provides the framework for setting them. Confirmed.
citations_verified_before_sending.4.3: c) interfaces and dependencies between activities performed by the organization, and those performed by other organizations. Confirmed, and 4.3 is the scope clause.
citations_verified_before_sending.9.3: 9.3.1 planned intervals; 9.3.2 inputs a)-g); 9.3.3 results shall include decisions related to continual improvement. Confirmed.
citations_verified_before_sending.4.1 climate: The Amd 1:2024 text is indexed and contains 'climate change'. The proposal names no clause number.

rows_detail.instrument: leak gate: union 1.000 against ISO/IEC 27000:2018 cl.3 - a COMPLETE reproduction split by the omitted 'or disclosed'. tier-A.
rows_detail.current: information is not made available to unauthorized individuals, entities or processes
rows_detail.proposed: Information reaching only those cleared to see it. The property a breach destroys permanently - availability comes back after an outage, but nothing un-discloses what has already left.

rows_detail.current: the boundaries and applicability of the ISMS
rows_detail.proposed: What the management system covers and what it leaves out, decided from the context and the interested parties. Whatever falls outside is outside the risk assessment, the controls and the certificate too.

rows_detail.current: the requirement to determine whether climate change is a relevant issue
rows_detail.proposed: The 2024 amendment made every organization decide whether climate change bears on its ISMS, and record the decision. Answering no is permitted; not answering is the nonconformity.

rows_detail.instrument: leak gate: 0.714 against ISO/IEC 27002:2022, exempt as title class - rewritten anyway because a control-theme name teaches nothing.
rows_detail.current: controls governing information security in supplier relationships
rows_detail.proposed: Security obligations that travel with the relationship instead of stopping at the signature: what a supplier must do, and how the organization keeps checking it is still being done.

rows_detail.instrument: leak gate: 0.667 against ISO/IEC 27000:2018, exempt as title class.
rows_detail.current: implementation guidance for the reference controls
rows_detail.proposed: The companion that explains how each Annex A control is meant to work, with a purpose and guidance for every one. Advisory only: an organization is certified against 27001, never against this.

rows_detail.instrument: tier-A defined term. No gate fire.
rows_detail.current: restricting access to information and processing facilities
rows_detail.proposed: Deciding who may reach which information, and enforcing it. The control most often right on the day it is granted and wrong six months later, because roles move and permissions rarely follow.

rows_detail.current: the requirements against which conformity is judged
rows_detail.proposed: The reference an auditor compares evidence against - the standard, the organization's own policies, its contracts and the law. Naming them is what separates a finding from an opinion.

rows_detail.current: the ongoing obligation to improve suitability, adequacy and effectiveness
rows_detail.proposed: A standing obligation to keep the system fit for its purpose, not a project with an end date. It is judged on whether something actually changed, never on whether improvement was intended.

rows_detail.instrument: tier-A defined term. Zero runs against the index today.
rows_detail.current: information is accurate and complete and has not been altered without authorization
rows_detail.proposed: Information staying accurate and complete unless someone authorised changes it. The property whose failure is hardest to spot: corrupted data looks exactly like correct data until something depends on it.

rows_detail.current: understanding the nature of a risk and determining its level
rows_detail.proposed: Working out how likely a risk is and how much it would cost, to arrive at a level. This stage produces the number; deciding whether that number is tolerable belongs to the next one.

rows_detail.current: comparing analysis results against criteria to decide significance
rows_detail.proposed: Comparing an analysed risk against the criteria to decide whether it needs treating. The stage where the organization's own thresholds do the work, which is why criteria written afterwards are worth nothing.

rows_detail.current: the person accountable for a specific risk and its treatment
rows_detail.proposed: The person with authority to accept a risk and answerable for how it is treated. Naming one is what stops a register becoming a list of things nobody has agreed to do anything about.

rows_detail.current: the documented record of which controls are necessary and why
rows_detail.proposed: The record of which controls are necessary, why, and whether they are in place. An auditor reads it as reasoning rather than a tick-list, so an entry carrying no justification is itself the finding.

rows_detail.current: the level at which ISMS accountability ultimately sits
rows_detail.proposed: Whoever can direct resources and set direction at the top of the scope - not necessarily the board, and not necessarily the whole company. Several clause 5 duties cannot be delegated away from them.

rows_detail.instrument: one-line label on a teachable concept.
rows_detail.current: a systematic, documented approach to managing information security risk
rows_detail.proposed: A managed set of policies, processes and controls for information security risk, with the weight on managed. What separates it from a collection of good security measures is that this one is planned, checked and improved.

rows_detail.current: the defined roles that carry ISMS responsibilities
rows_detail.proposed: Who does what in the system, written down. Undefined roles are the usual reason an obligation everyone agrees with turns out to have been performed by nobody.

rows_detail.current: the documented statement of intent and direction
rows_detail.proposed: Top management's statement of intent that everything else hangs from. Clause 5.2 requires it to set the objectives or provide the framework for setting them, so a policy committing to nothing measurable fails on its own terms.

rows_detail.instrument: one-line label. CITES CLAUSE 5.1 AND A COUNT.
rows_detail.current: top management's demonstrable ownership of the ISMS
rows_detail.proposed: Shown through decisions, resourcing and attention rather than a signed statement. Clause 5.1 lists eight specific things top management must do, which is what makes the commitment auditable at all.

rows_detail.current: the persons and organizations with a stake in the ISMS
rows_detail.proposed: Anyone with a stake in the organization's information security - customers, regulators, staff, suppliers. They are determined before the scope, because what they require feeds into what the scope has to cover.

rows_detail.instrument: one-line label. CITES CLAUSE 4.1 AND THE 2024 AMENDMENT.
rows_detail.current: the factors that affect the organization's ability to achieve its security objectives
rows_detail.proposed: The conditions that help or hinder the ISMS reaching its objectives. Clause 4.1 asks the organization to determine them, and the 2024 amendment added climate change as one it must explicitly consider.

rows_detail.current: the internal and external setting in which the ISMS operates
rows_detail.proposed: The setting the system has to work in, established before anything is designed. Get it wrong and every downstream decision - scope, risks, controls - is calibrated against an organization that does not exist.

rows_detail.current: what is inside and outside the system being managed
rows_detail.proposed: Where the system stops. An unstated boundary is read as coverage, so anything left vague resolves in the reader's favour and against the organization.

rows_detail.current: the points where in-scope activities meet out-of-scope ones
rows_detail.proposed: Where in-scope activity touches something outside the scope. Clause 4.3 requires them to be considered when the scope is set, because a boundary that ignores its own crossings describes nothing.

rows_detail.current: the requirement that a determined change to the ISMS be carried out in a planned manner
rows_detail.proposed: Changes to the ISMS are meant to be carried out deliberately rather than noticed afterwards. The requirement is about the manner of the change, which is why an undocumented improvement can still be a nonconformity.

rows_detail.instrument: one-line label. Fires only on a RAW union (0.667 from two commonplaces four words apart) and is correctly rejected by the source-side conditions.
rows_detail.current: plan-do-check-act as the improvement rhythm of a management system
rows_detail.proposed: Plan, do, check, act as the rhythm the whole standard is built on - clauses 6 and 7 plan, 8 does, 9 checks, 10 acts. The point is that improvement runs continuously instead of arriving as a phase at the end.

rows_detail.current: anything of value to the organization that holds or processes information
rows_detail.proposed: Anything holding or processing information the organization would mind losing. The register is where AI tooling usually escapes, because nobody thinks of a browser tab as an asset.

rows_detail.current: authenticity, non-repudiation, accountability and reliability as properties supporting the triad
rows_detail.proposed: Authenticity, non-repudiation, accountability and reliability - what makes the triad usable in practice. A system can be perfectly confidential and still useless if nobody can prove who did what.

rows_detail.current: how a threat exploiting a vulnerability against an asset produces risk, and how a control modifies it
rows_detail.proposed: A threat exploiting a vulnerability against an asset is what produces a risk, and a control changes one of those terms. Getting the composition right is what makes a risk assessable instead of a worry.

rows_detail.current: an identified occurrence indicating a possible security-relevant state
rows_detail.proposed: Something observed that might matter to security - a failed login, an alert, an unexpected transfer. Most events are nothing, and the reason for recording them is that you cannot tell which until you look.

rows_detail.current: one or more events that compromise operations or threaten information security
rows_detail.proposed: One or more events that actually threaten operations or information. The line between event and incident is a judgement somebody has to make, and the response process starts at the moment they make it.

rows_detail.current: an incident resulting in unauthorized disclosure of information
rows_detail.proposed: An incident where information reached someone who should not have it. The subset that usually starts a legal reporting clock, which is why it is named apart from the general case.

rows_detail.instrument: one of the four treatment options.
rows_detail.current: applying controls to change likelihood or consequence
rows_detail.proposed: Applying controls to change how likely a risk is or how much it would cost. The commonest treatment by far, and the only one that keeps the activity running and leaves the risk on the register.

rows_detail.instrument: one of the four treatment options.
rows_detail.current: transferring or sharing risk with another party
rows_detail.proposed: Moving part of the consequence to someone else - insurance, a supplier, a contract term. What transfers is the cost; the accountability never does, and an auditor will look for exactly that distinction.

rows_detail.current: choosing a defensible treatment for an identified risk
rows_detail.proposed: Choosing among the four options and being able to defend the choice. Defensible means traceable back to the stated criteria, not merely reasonable once the outcome is known.

rows_detail.current: the plan for implementing selected treatment
rows_detail.proposed: What will be done, by whom, by when, and what the risk looks like afterwards. Deciding a treatment and planning it are separate steps, and a plan with no owner or date is the usual finding.

rows_detail.current: the thresholds at which a risk may be retained
rows_detail.proposed: The thresholds saying which risks may be lived with. Set alongside the assessment criteria and before any results arrive, or acceptance stops being a policy and becomes a decision taken one risk at a time.

rows_detail.current: the risk owner's acceptance of residual risk and the treatment plan
rows_detail.proposed: The risk owner has to accept both the plan and the residual risk it will leave behind. That acceptance is what converts an analysis into an organizational decision somebody is answerable for.

rows_detail.current: a control applied where the preferred one is unavailable
rows_detail.proposed: A different control used where the expected one cannot be. Legitimate when the risk still moves; the failure is offering the substitution itself as the justification without showing any effect.

rows_detail.current: controls are selected because risk treatment requires them
rows_detail.proposed: Controls come from what the risk treatment needs, not from working down Annex A. Selecting first and justifying afterwards produces a Statement of Applicability that records a checklist rather than a decision.

rows_detail.current: top management's periodic review of the ISMS
rows_detail.proposed: Top management examining whether the ISMS is still working, at planned intervals. Clause 9.3 fixes what must go in and what must come out, so a review that records no decisions has not happened.
